glosses: To keep repeating a particular sound involuntarily during speech.
To utter with a stammer, or with timid hesitancy.

examples.text: He blushed, and stammered a few words of apology.

glosses: The involuntary repetition of a sound in speech.

examples.text: She said goodbye in a stammer.

glosses: A speech defect whereby someone speaks with a stammer
To speak unintelligibly or inaudibly; to fail to articulate.

examples.text: Please try not to mumble so I can hear you better.

glosses: To chew something gently with closed lips.

examples.text: All I could hear was a mumble from the next room.

glosses: An unsteadiness.

examples.text: Tom, who isn't paying much attention, is suddenly caught by the falter in his voice as he reads the two lines—

examples.text: He found his legs falter.

examples.text: And remember, comrades, your resolution must never falter.

It was important that there be no hesitancy on my part — nothing to indicate that the U.S. government had faltered. Eisenhower, and John F. Kennedy — policies of firmness on the one hand and an effort to thaw the Cold War on the other.
